the level of trust in the courts in Poland has decreased in the period of 2015 to 2018; the level of trust is very low and is lower than the level of trust for the Sejm and President; there are differences in the levels of trust in the court between political parties' voters; and, finally, the campaign Just courts ( Sprawiedliwe Sady) has had a positive effect on the level of trust of the courts among its participants.
the Polish society is very divided in its attitude towards the judiciary.
the level of trust in the judiciary has decreased significantly since 2015, but it varies depending on age and education.

the question: How did Polish citizens react to the Constitutional Crisis and how has their trust in the judiciary changed over the past three years?
the question of how Polish society has been reacting to the judicial reforms and how the public perception of the courts has been changing in recent years.
the question: how did Polish citizens' trust in the judiciary change during the period of judicial reforms?

the Polish society is not homogeneous, and it is not possible to speak about the average citizen.
there is a significant difference between the average citizen's opinion and the opinion of the elites.
Polish citizens trust in the judiciary has been declining since 2015 and the campaign Just courts has not been effective in increasing the level of public trust in this institution.

the judiciary is perceived as a trustworthy institution by Polish society, but it seems that this perception has changed over time and the changes are related to the events that have occurred in Poland since the beginning of the Constitutional crisis.
